verdict.rationale: Rev AI's Asynchronous Speech-to-Text API is documented as transcribing an audio file the user submits, and it publishes accepted formats (all FFmpeg formats, including MP3, MP4, Ogg, WAV and FLAC) and a 17-hour duration cap. The quoted 5 TB size limit covers only dashboard uploads and source_config jobs, so the limit for direct local-file API upload is not evidenced. missing for 10: explicit documentation of the local-file upload endpoint (path/multipart method), a published size limit for direct local API uploads, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can submit a local audio or video file for transcription through a documented API endpoint, with accepted formats and size limits published

citations.quote: This tutorial uses the Asynchronous Speech to Text API to produce a transcript of an audio file submitted by you.
The Asynchronous Speech-to-Text API supports all the file formats supported by FFmpeg. This includes common media formats such as MP3, MP4, Ogg, WAV, PCM and FLAC
Maximum audio duration of 17 hours... File uploads via the Rev AI dashboard or using the source_config job parameter have a file size limit of 5 TB.
